source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Once privileges are granted, subsequent performance data are irrelevant because competence is assumed permanently unless the practitioner changes employers.","B":"Ongoing evaluation exists only to verify payroll and scheduling records and is not used in decisions about clinical privileges or focused review.","C":"Recredentialing requires one universal federal renewal interval for every practitioner and facility, so performance data need not be reviewed between cycles.","D":"Ongoing professional practice evaluation supplies current performance data that inform continued privileges and whether focused review or action is needed."}}
source_row.rationale: Ongoing professional practice evaluation provides current competency/performance evidence for privileging decisions and can trigger focused review; a universal one-to-two-year recredentialing interval should not be substituted for the actual OPPE requirement.
source_row.source_detail: OPPE FAQ explains that ongoing professional practice evaluation provides information to determine whether to continue, limit or revoke privileges and whether focused professional practice evaluation is warranted. Joint Commission Standards FAQ updated January 7, 2026; rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: The Joint Commission — Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE)
source_row.stem: Why does a hospital continue evaluating a practitioner's professional performance after privileges have been granted?
